judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 6 Indicators (same statement grain, same canonical Grade rank 2) in Strand 4: Data, Sub-strand 1 (Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis), under different Content Standards: B6.4.1.1 (create, label and interpret line graphs) and B6.4.1.2 (select, justify and use appropriate methods of collecting data). B6.4.1.1.2 is a representational judgement — decide whether a data set suits a line graph (continuous) or a series of points (discrete) and explain why — with LCs on data representation and reasoned justification. B6.4.1.2.3 is a questionnaire investigation — design, administer, record, analyse and graph results to solve problems. The two are substantively coherent: choosing and justifying how data should be displayed sits alongside collecting, analysing and graphing one's own data, so they mutually reinforce the sub-strand's data-handling cycle beyond mere shared ancestry, the weak 'b6/4/1' code prefix, or 'data'/'graph' token overlap. But no developmental dependency is evidenced at equal rank: B6.4.1.2.3's graphing and analysis LCs are generic and never invoke the continuous/discrete distinction, the two indicators sit under sibling Content Standards with no stated ordering, and the rank-proximity signal is explicitly weak with rank_gap 0. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the correct complete judgment. Evidence limitations: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, including the merged case-variant BASIC 6 Grade organizer; these remain unresolved.

B6.1.1.1 (Sub-Strand 1: Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality) establishes quantity and place-value understanding of multi-digit whole numerals, with bounded source context showing indicators for reading/writing, comparing and ordering whole numbers and skip counting forwards and backwards. B6.1.2.6 (Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations) extends the number system to integers, with bounded source context showing indicators for locating, comparing and ordering integers on the number line with '<' and '>' and simple operations with integers. Shared tokens ('demonstrate an understanding of') and the common B6.1 code prefix were not treated as evidence. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same canonical coordinate rank 2) within Strand 1: Number, but in different Sub-Strands: B6.1.1.1 addresses quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1 billion (Counting, Representation, Cardinality & Ordinality), while B6.1.2.5 addresses translating word problems into mathematical sentences and solving them (Number Operations, with source context indicating multi-step problems across the four operations). The two are substantively coherent: whole-number magnitude and place-value understanding is reinforced when learners model and compute within word problems. However, the target's core demand is modelling/translation of problem situations rather than an extension of place-value understanding, and at equal grade rank the supplied evidence (shared Strand/Grade ancestry, weak code-prefix and token/trigram overlap of only generic tokens such as 'and') does not substantively establish that proficiency in one underwrites success in the other, so a symmetric relation is the supported judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated, so unseen indicator detail could alter the picture.
